title: Sequence cohort routing with kernel affinity and decode spacing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a runtime component that groups incoming requests into sequence-length cohorts, routes cohorts to kernels with matching affinity, and introduces decode-spacing heuristics that interleave prefill and decode work to reduce padding waste while preserving low tail latency. This ticket focuses on the policy and scheduling layer (cohort creation, kernel affinity hints, and decode spacing), not the kernel implementations themselves.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiments show >=15% reduction in average padding tokens for mixed-length workloads compared to baseline fixed-bucketing.
P95 decode latency for short-prefill-heavy traffic does not regress more than 5% under typical production load profile.
New cohort router exposes telemetry: cohort-size distribution, kernel-affinity assignments, padding-saved estimate, and decode-spacing idleness metric.
Changes covered by unit tests, integration test harness, and a canary rollout plan in dedicated pool.
design_notes: Cohort semantics: group requests into ephemeral cohorts based on 'effective compute length' which is sequence length + estimated decode budget; cohorts close either by size or by small timeout (configurable 5-20ms).

Kernel affinity: runtime uses a small learned lookup (sigmoid-scored) that maps (seq_len_bucket, model_variant, hardware_type) -> preferred kernel candidate. Affinity is a hint; fallback allowed if preferred kernel queue depth exceeds threshold.

Decode spacing: instead of strictly waiting for prefill to finish for all cohort members, allow staggered prefill+decode for longer requests so short requests in the same cohort can start decoding earlier; guarantees kept by KV-cache ownership tokens to avoid race conditions.

Attention optimizations interplay: favor kernels that expose fused-attention paths when cohort sequence distributions indicate high attention compute (wide sequences), otherwise prefer tiled/gemm-favoring kernels for many short sequences.

Budgeting trade-off: aggressive cohorting reduces padding but can increase per-request latency for low-volume short requests; we bias router with a latency-weight to protect p95 for latency-sensitive orgs/configurations.
implementation_plan: 1) Add cohort router module to runtime request path; implement ephemeral cohort lifecycle and config knobs (timeout, min_size, max_size).
2) Surface kernel-affinity table and scoring function; wire to compiler/kernel registry for runtime hints.

3) Implement decode-spacing scheduler that can preemptively start decode for cohort members with short effective remaining tokens while other members are still pre-filling. Use KV-cache locks with ownership tokens.
4) Add telemetry events and metrics (cohort_open, cohort_close, affinity_chosen, padding_saved_estimate, decode_spacing_saturated).
5) Integration tests with workload harness and synthetic mix of short/medium/long sequences, then run canary on dedicated pool.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed for cohort lifecycle semantics; timeout=12ms and min_size=8 chosen as default after microbenchmarks on p4d cluster.
2026-02-18: Prototype kernel-affinity table integrated with compiler registry; initial mapping favors fused-attention kernel for >1024 tokens on A100 and tiled kernels for <256 tokens.

2026-02-24: Discovered race condition in KV-cache ownership when decode spacing starts earlier than prefill end for another shard; mitigated with ownership token plus per-shard fence. Patch in PR #2873.

2026-03-01: Benchmarks using mixed traffic (40% short, 40% medium, 20% long) show 18% padding token reduction and 3% mean latency improvement; p95 for short requests increased by 4.2% — within target.
2026-03-05: Canary rollout scheduled for 24h in dedicated-small pool; telemetry hooks and alert thresholds configured.
test_plan: Unit tests for cohort open/close edge cases and kernel-affinity scoring correctness.
Integration harness includes: synthetic traffic generator with configurable seqlen distribution; assertion that padding_saved_estimate >= 10% for heavy-mix workloads.
Stress test with bursty arrival patterns and node failover to ensure graceful fallback to default single-shot execution.
Performance regression tests comparing baseline runtime-1.21 and new runtime-1.22 with stable seed for kernels.
risks: Increased scheduling complexity may introduce subtle priority inversions across latency tiers; mitigated by latency-weight in router and fairness queues.
Kernel affinity hints could reduce utilization if the registry mappings are stale; plan to periodically re-evaluate affinities via nightly microbenchmarks.
Decode spacing requires careful KV-cache fencing — incorrect fences may lead to corrupted caches or incorrect token outputs; extensive integration tests required.
next_steps: Merge PR #2873 after final review and run 24h canary in dedicated-small pool.
Instrument additional per-customer telemetry flags for latency protection and allow per-account policy toggles.
Plan follow-up ticket to add an online learning loop that adjusts kernel-affinity scores based on observed latency/cost trade-offs.
